title: Short uncompletable words bounded by maximum codeword length
formal: For every finite incomplete variable-length code X, is there an uncompletable word of length polynomial in k=max{length(x): x∈X}, with a polynomial independent of X?
context:
An uncompletable word is not a factor of any word in X*. The weaker polynomial bound in the total length of X was proved by Kiefer and Mascle in 2019; only the maximum-word-length target is retained. The original 2k² Restivo bound for arbitrary finite sets is false.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Tests how long a missing factor can remain hidden when the dictionary has unique factorization.
